name: OWASP WebGoat
intendedUse: The README describes WebGoat as a deliberately insecure web application maintained by OWASP to teach web application security, not to be exposed: https://github.com/WebGoat/WebGoat/blob/7e198f39189f33e1912f7cbb60e24e42635ca06a/README.md

image.note: WebGoat is served under the /WebGoat context path (paths below include it). Every lesson endpoint needs a logged-in session; anyone can register at /WebGoat/registration. WebWolf (companion app in the same image) is out of scope. The real Spring actuator (/WebGoat/actuator/env, health, configprops) is permitAll at this ref but is not a documented lesson item, so it is not listed.

builtBy: Claude (AI-assisted), from the WebGoat v2026.5 lesson sources (assignment endpoints) and lesson pages; to be checked by labeller A

vulnerabilities.title: WebGoat introduction: mail
vulnerabilities.description: Introductory exercise sending a test mail to WebWolf; teaches tooling only.
vulnerabilities.note: Mapped at /WebGoat/mail* inside the /WebGoat context, so the full path repeats the prefix.

vulnerabilities.title: WebWolf introduction
vulnerabilities.description: Introduction to the WebWolf companion app (mailbox, landing page).
vulnerabilities.note: WebWolf is out of scope for this benchmark.

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Basics
vulnerabilities.description: Tutorial on HTTP requests and methods, with a quiz; nothing vulnerable.

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Basics: external request
vulnerabilities.description: Exercise sending a PUT request from an external tool; teaches tooling only.

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Proxies: intercept request
vulnerabilities.description: Exercise on intercepting and modifying a request with a proxy; teaches tooling only.

vulnerabilities.title: Developer Tools
vulnerabilities.description: Exercises using browser developer tools console and network tab; teaches tooling only.

vulnerabilities.title: CIA Triad quiz
vulnerabilities.description: Quiz on confidentiality, integrity and availability.

vulnerabilities.title: Writing new lesson (template)
vulnerabilities.description: Sample lesson showing contributors how to write a lesson; not a vulnerability exercise.

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Parameter Pollution: observation
vulnerabilities.description: Shows how components read duplicate parameters differently; output is escaped, nothing to exploit.

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Parameter Pollution: transfer
vulnerabilities.description: Validation checks the first recipient parameter but the transfer uses the last one.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (intro): SQL basics (DML/DDL/DCL)
vulnerabilities.description: Learner-typed SQL statements are executed to teach SELECT, UPDATE, ALTER and GRANT syntax.
vulnerabilities.note: Deliberate SQL console for syntax practice; it does run request SQL, so a scanner hit here is debatable.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (intro): string SQL injection
vulnerabilities.description: Last-name parameter concatenated into a SELECT on user_data; tautology returns all rows.
vulnerabilities.note: POST params account, operator, injection are concatenated together.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (intro): numeric SQL injection
vulnerabilities.description: userid parameter concatenated unquoted into a partly prepared SELECT.
vulnerabilities.note: POST param userid (login_count is bound).

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (intro): compromising confidentiality
vulnerabilities.description: Name and TAN concatenated into employee query; string injection dumps all employees.
vulnerabilities.note: POST params name, auth_tan.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (intro): compromising integrity (query chaining)
vulnerabilities.description: Same concatenated employee query allows chained UPDATE statements to change salaries.
vulnerabilities.note: POST params name, auth_tan.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (intro): compromising availability
vulnerabilities.description: Search term concatenated into LIKE query on access_log; chaining lets attacker drop the table.
vulnerabilities.note: POST param action_string.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (advanced): UNION / pulling data from other tables
vulnerabilities.description: Last-name parameter concatenated into SELECT; UNION or chaining reads user_system_data passwords.
vulnerabilities.note: POST param userid_6a. Follow-up /SqlInjectionAdvanced/attack6b only checks the recovered password (see sqli-adv-6b-answer).

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (advanced): submit Dave's password
vulnerabilities.description: Answer check for the password obtained through the 6a injection.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (advanced): blind injection in registration
vulnerabilities.description: Registration username concatenated into existence check; boolean-based blind injection reveals Tom's password.
vulnerabilities.note: PUT with username_reg/email_reg/password_reg; only a true/false 'user exists' signal. The login form (/SqlInjectionAdvanced/login, prepared statement) is where the recovered password is used.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (advanced): quiz
vulnerabilities.description: Quiz on prepared statements and injection.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (mitigation): write safe code
vulnerabilities.description: Fill-in and code-editor exercises writing prepared statements; nothing vulnerable.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (mitigation): ORDER BY injection
vulnerabilities.description: Sort column parameter appended to ORDER BY in the servers list; blind injection reveals a server IP.
vulnerabilities.note: GET param column on the helper endpoint; the scored /SqlInjectionMitigations/attack12a only checks the recovered IP (prepared statement).

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (mitigation): input validation alone (no spaces)
vulnerabilities.description: Rejects spaces then reuses the 6a concatenated query; comments replace spaces to inject.
vulnerabilities.note: Filter bypass needed; underlying sink is the same as sqli-adv-6a-union.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (mitigation): input validation on keywords
vulnerabilities.description: Strips SELECT/FROM once and rejects spaces; doubled keywords and comments still inject.
vulnerabilities.note: Filter bypass needed; underlying sink is the same as sqli-adv-6a-union.

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection: safety acknowledgement
vulnerabilities.description: Learner confirms commands will run on the host before tasks unlock.

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection: recognise the wrapper
vulnerabilities.description: Learner reproduces the shell command string a ping wrapper would build; nothing executes.
vulnerabilities.note: Simulated: the endpoint only pattern-matches the expected answer; nothing real to observe.

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection: command chaining
vulnerabilities.description: Payload appended to a base command and run through the shell; chaining leaks an environment token.
vulnerabilities.note: POST params base, payload. Requires the per-user safety acknowledgement (POST /WebGoat/CommandInjection/safety) first, otherwise 403.

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection: command chaining (source sink)
vulnerabilities.description: Request payload concatenated into a shell command executed via ProcessBuilder sh -c.
vulnerabilities.note: Java: Penthera's repo route analysis reads JS/TS only.

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection: cat search (grep)
vulnerabilities.description: Search title concatenated into a grep shell command; injection reads a per-user flag file.
vulnerabilities.note: POST param title. Requires the safety acknowledgement first. /CommandInjection/task3/flag only checks the exfiltrated flag.

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection: cat search (source sink)
vulnerabilities.description: Title string concatenated into 'grep ... images/*.txt' and run through the shell.
vulnerabilities.note: Java: Penthera's repo route analysis reads JS/TS only.

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection: bypass a deny-list
vulnerabilities.description: Search strips ; && | then runs grep via shell; other metacharacters still inject.
vulnerabilities.note: Filter bypass needed (e.g. $() or newline). Sink in CommandInjectionTask4Service.java. /CommandInjection/task4/key only checks the exfiltrated key.

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection: evaluate mitigations
vulnerabilities.description: Learner picks execution mode, allow-list and sanitiser; server shows which configuration blocks injection.

vulnerabilities.title: Cross Site Scripting: try it in the console
vulnerabilities.description: Learner compares document.cookie across tabs; introductory, nothing vulnerable.

vulnerabilities.title: Cross Site Scripting: reflected XSS in shopping cart
vulnerabilities.description: Credit-card field echoed unescaped into the purchase confirmation HTML.
vulnerabilities.note: GET params QTY1-4 (integers, required) and field1 (reflected). Reflection sits in the JSON 'output' field, which the lesson page inserts as HTML.

vulnerabilities.title: Cross Site Scripting: DOM-based XSS (test route)
vulnerabilities.description: Leftover client-side test route writes the URL fragment parameter into the page as HTML.
vulnerabilities.note: Payload lives in the fragment (#test/...), never reaches the server. Scored endpoints /CrossSiteScripting/attack6a, /phone-home-xss and /dom-follow-up only check answers.

vulnerabilities.title: Cross Site Scripting: DOM-based XSS (source sink)
vulnerabilities.description: showTestParam passes the route parameter to jQuery .html() without encoding.
vulnerabilities.note: Route wired in GoatRouter.js / LessonController.js.

vulnerabilities.title: Cross Site Scripting: quiz
vulnerabilities.description: Quiz on XSS concepts.

vulnerabilities.title: Cross Site Scripting (stored): blog comments
vulnerabilities.description: Comment text is stored and later rendered into other users' comment list as HTML.
vulnerabilities.note: /CrossSiteScriptingStored/stored-xss-follow-up only checks the phoned-home value.

vulnerabilities.title: Cross Site Scripting (stored): comment rendering sink
vulnerabilities.description: Comment list built by string-replacing raw comment text into HTML and appended with jQuery.

vulnerabilities.title: Cross Site Scripting (mitigation): encode output / sanitise input
vulnerabilities.description: Exercises writing JSP encoding and AntiSamy code; nothing vulnerable.

vulnerabilities.title: XXE: simple XXE in comment
vulnerabilities.description: Comment XML parsed with external entities enabled; entity reads the file system.

vulnerabilities.title: XXE: modern REST framework (content-type switch)
vulnerabilities.description: JSON comment endpoint also accepts XML when the content type is changed, then resolves entities.

vulnerabilities.title: XXE: blind XXE data exfiltration
vulnerabilities.description: Blind XXE where file contents are exfiltrated through an attacker-hosted DTD.
vulnerabilities.note: Also needs WebWolf/an external server.

vulnerabilities.title: Path Traversal: profile upload (full name in path)
vulnerabilities.description: Uploaded file stored using user-supplied name, allowing writes outside the intended directory.

vulnerabilities.title: Path Traversal: profile upload with ../ filter
vulnerabilities.description: Single-pass removal of ../ from the name is bypassed with nested sequences.

vulnerabilities.title: Path Traversal: upload using original file name
vulnerabilities.description: Uploaded file's original filename is used as path, so a crafted multipart name traverses.

vulnerabilities.title: Path Traversal: retrieving other files
vulnerabilities.description: Random-picture id parameter used as file path after a bypassable filter; reads files outside image folder.

vulnerabilities.title: Path Traversal: Zip Slip
vulnerabilities.description: Zip entries extracted without checking names, so ../ entries overwrite files elsewhere.

vulnerabilities.title: Open Redirect: unvalidated redirect endpoint
vulnerabilities.description: Redirects with a 302 to any URL given in the url parameter.
vulnerabilities.note: GET param url. Linked from the lesson page as the 'real (unsafe) redirect' to experiment with; tasks 1-4 are simulated.

vulnerabilities.title: Open Redirect: task 1
vulnerabilities.description: Simulated check that an absolute external URL would be redirected to without validation.
vulnerabilities.note: Simulated: the endpoint only pattern-matches the expected answer; nothing real to observe. No redirect is issued.

vulnerabilities.title: Open Redirect: task 2
vulnerabilities.description: Simulated naive substring filter for 'webgoat' that an external host can still satisfy.
vulnerabilities.note: Simulated: the endpoint only pattern-matches the expected answer; nothing real to observe. No redirect is issued.

vulnerabilities.title: Open Redirect: task 3
vulnerabilities.description: Simulated startsWith host check bypassable with userinfo (@) or crafted subdomains.
vulnerabilities.note: Simulated: the endpoint only pattern-matches the expected answer; nothing real to observe. No redirect is issued.

vulnerabilities.title: Open Redirect: task 4
vulnerabilities.description: Simulated single-decode validation bypassable with double URL encoding.
vulnerabilities.note: Simulated: the endpoint only pattern-matches the expected answer; nothing real to observe. No redirect is issued.

vulnerabilities.title: Open Redirect: mitigation check
vulnerabilities.description: Learner shows that an external redirect would be blocked by the safe pattern.

vulnerabilities.title: Open Redirect: quiz
vulnerabilities.description: Quiz on open redirects.

vulnerabilities.title: SSRF: change the requested image
vulnerabilities.description: Learner changes the image URL parameter from Tom to Jerry; server only matches the string.
vulnerabilities.note: Simulated: the endpoint only pattern-matches the expected answer; nothing real to observe.

vulnerabilities.title: SSRF: make the server fetch an external URL
vulnerabilities.description: Server fetches the URL parameter, but only the exact value http://ifconfig.pro is fetched.
vulnerabilities.note: Allow-listed to one external host via regex; any other URL is not fetched, so a generic SSRF probe sees nothing.

vulnerabilities.title: Vulnerable Components: jquery-ui 1.10.x closeText XSS
vulnerabilities.description: Lesson loads an old jquery-ui whose dialog closeText option allows XSS, beside a fixed version.
vulnerabilities.note: Static /js/** is permitAll. Lesson text calls it jquery-ui:1.10.4; the file's banner says v1.10.3.

vulnerabilities.title: Vulnerable Components: jQuery 2.1.4 used for the vulnerable demo
vulnerabilities.description: jQuery 2.1.4 is loaded as the 'vulnerable' jQuery instance backing the jquery-ui demo.
vulnerabilities.note: Not named in the lesson text; included because main.js wires it as 'jqueryvuln' for the documented demo. Drop if labeller disagrees.

vulnerabilities.title: Vulnerable Components: XStream deserialization (CVE-2013-7285)
vulnerabilities.description: Contact XML parsed by XStream 1.4.5; a dynamic-proxy payload executes code.
vulnerabilities.note: Server-side dependency pinned in pom.xml (xstream.version 1.4.5).

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Deserialization
vulnerabilities.description: Base64 Java serialized object from the request is deserialized; a crafted gadget delays the server.

vulnerabilities.title: CSRF: basic GET request
vulnerabilities.description: Flag endpoint accepts a cross-site form post without token, only checking the Referer.

vulnerabilities.title: CSRF: post a review on someone's behalf
vulnerabilities.description: Review submission protected only by a static hidden value and Referer check.

vulnerabilities.title: CSRF: JSON feedback
vulnerabilities.description: Feedback endpoint accepts JSON sent as text/plain from a cross-site form.

vulnerabilities.title: CSRF: login CSRF
vulnerabilities.description: Victim is logged into an attacker-created account through a forged login request.

vulnerabilities.title: Security Misconfiguration: default credentials
vulnerabilities.description: Staging admin console still accepts the factory default admin/admin login.

vulnerabilities.title: Security Misconfiguration: verbose error
vulnerabilities.description: Error endpoint returns a stack trace including environment, database password and API token.
vulnerabilities.note: Plain-text stack trace served with 200 at a lesson-specific path (linked from the lesson page JS). /task2 and /task2/config only check the token.

vulnerabilities.title: Security Misconfiguration: verbose error (secrets in source)
vulnerabilities.description: The leaked database password and API token are string literals in the Java source.
vulnerabilities.note: Training placeholders (DB_PASSWORD, SYSTEM_API_TOKEN).

vulnerabilities.title: Security Misconfiguration: exposed actuator env
vulnerabilities.description: Mock actuator env endpoint returns configuration including an internal API key.
vulnerabilities.note: Lesson-specific mock under the lesson path, not Spring's real /actuator. /task3/actuator/health is harmless; /task3 only checks the key.

vulnerabilities.title: Security Misconfiguration: exposed actuator env (key in source)
vulnerabilities.description: The leaked internal API key is a string literal in the Java source.
vulnerabilities.note: Training placeholder value; may not match generic key patterns.

vulnerabilities.title: Security Misconfiguration: harden the configuration
vulnerabilities.description: Learner submits the settings that disable debug endpoints and default users.

vulnerabilities.title: Password Storage: unsalted SHA-256
vulnerabilities.description: Leaked unsalted fast hashes are cracked with a wordlist.

vulnerabilities.title: Password Storage: salted fast hash
vulnerabilities.description: Per-user salts hide equal passwords but fast hashes stay crackable.

vulnerabilities.title: Password Storage: Argon2 parameters and pepper
vulnerabilities.description: Learner reads Argon2 parameters and explains why a pepper is needed; nothing vulnerable.

vulnerabilities.title: Password Storage: disclosed configuration backup
vulnerabilities.description: A blog backup application.properties is served, revealing the password pepper.
vulnerabilities.note: Scored at /PasswordStorage/stage5 (answer check).

vulnerabilities.title: Password Storage: pepper hardcoded in source
vulnerabilities.description: The pepper served in the backup file is a hardcoded constant in Java source.
vulnerabilities.note: Training placeholder value.

vulnerabilities.title: Crypto Basics: Base64 basic auth
vulnerabilities.description: Basic-auth header is only Base64 encoded; learner decodes the credentials.

vulnerabilities.title: Crypto Basics: XOR encoding
vulnerabilities.description: WebSphere-style XOR-encoded password is trivially decoded.

vulnerabilities.title: Crypto Basics: plain hashes
vulnerabilities.description: Unsalted MD5/SHA-256 hashes of common words are reversed.

vulnerabilities.title: Crypto Basics: signing with a given private key
vulnerabilities.description: Learner signs a value with an RSA private key handed out by the lesson.
vulnerabilities.note: The private key endpoint is part of the exercise, not a leak.

vulnerabilities.title: Crypto Basics: secure defaults (secret in container)
vulnerabilities.description: A secret file left in the Docker image with weak permissions must be found and decrypted.
vulnerabilities.note: Needs shell access to the running container.

vulnerabilities.title: Timing Attacks: discover a secret byte by timing
vulnerabilities.description: Early-exit comparison leaks how many leading bytes match through response time.

vulnerabilities.title: Timing Attacks: recover an HMAC tag
vulnerabilities.description: Non-constant-time HMAC check lets the tag be recovered byte by byte.

vulnerabilities.title: Timing Attacks: recover a tag under noise
vulnerabilities.description: Same timing leak with added jitter, requiring statistical sampling.

vulnerabilities.title: Timing Attacks: mitigation
vulnerabilities.description: Learner picks the constant-time comparison fix.

vulnerabilities.title: Hijack a session: predictable session ids
vulnerabilities.description: Lesson auth cookie values are sequential with timestamps, so a valid one can be predicted.
vulnerabilities.note: Predictable tokens; not a claimed check.

vulnerabilities.title: IDOR: authenticate as tom
vulnerabilities.description: Lesson step logging in with given credentials before the IDOR tasks.

vulnerabilities.title: IDOR: observe differences
vulnerabilities.description: Learner names the profile attributes hidden from the UI; answer check only.

vulnerabilities.title: IDOR: guess the direct profile path
vulnerabilities.description: Learner submits the RESTful profile URL for their own user id; answer check only.

vulnerabilities.title: IDOR: view another user's profile
vulnerabilities.description: Profile endpoint returns any user's profile for a numeric id in the path.
vulnerabilities.note: GET /WebGoat/IDOR/profile/{userId}; other user is 2342388. Only answers after the lesson login as tom (POST /WebGoat/IDOR/login with the credentials given in the lesson).

vulnerabilities.title: IDOR: edit another user's profile
vulnerabilities.description: PUT to another user's profile id changes their role and colour.
vulnerabilities.note: Write access with role escalation, beyond read IDOR.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Function Level AC: hidden menu items
vulnerabilities.description: Admin menu items are only hidden in the HTML; learner names them.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Function Level AC: user list without authorization
vulnerabilities.description: Admin user-list endpoint (JSON) is served to any logged-in user, exposing password hashes.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Function Level AC: create an admin user
vulnerabilities.description: User-creation endpoint accepts an admin flag from any user, bypassing the fixed list's check.

vulnerabilities.title: Spoofing an authentication cookie
vulnerabilities.description: Auth cookie is a reversible encoding of the username, so one for tom can be forged.
vulnerabilities.note: Weak/predictable token construction.

vulnerabilities.title: Authentication Bypasses: 2FA password reset
vulnerabilities.description: Security-question check passes when the answer parameters are renamed, skipping verification.

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Login: credentials in clear text
vulnerabilities.description: Page script posts hard-coded credentials unencrypted; learner sniffs them from the request.
vulnerabilities.note: Credentials only appear in a request the page JS sends; WebGoat itself runs on plain HTTP.

vulnerabilities.title: JWT tokens: decode a token
vulnerabilities.description: Learner decodes a JWT to read the username; introductory.

vulnerabilities.title: JWT tokens: votes reset with unsigned token
vulnerabilities.description: Voting endpoints accept a JWT with alg none, so admin claim can be forged.
vulnerabilities.note: Token in the access_token cookie (issued by GET /WebGoat/JWT/votings/login). POST /WebGoat/JWT/votings resets votes when admin=true.

vulnerabilities.title: JWT tokens: crack the signing key
vulnerabilities.description: Token is HMAC-signed with a dictionary word, so the key can be brute-forced offline.
vulnerabilities.note: Offline dictionary attack on the HS256 key; not alg=none or verification bypass.

vulnerabilities.title: JWT tokens: signing key candidates in source
vulnerabilities.description: The possible HMAC signing secrets are hardcoded in a Java array.
vulnerabilities.note: Short dictionary words; a generic secret detector may not flag them.

vulnerabilities.title: JWT tokens: refresh lesson accepts alg none
vulnerabilities.description: Checkout accepts an unsigned alg-none token for Tom; the lesson accepts this as a solution.
vulnerabilities.note: Authorization: Bearer header. Lesson feedback key jwt-refresh-alg-none.

vulnerabilities.title: JWT tokens: refresh someone else's token
vulnerabilities.description: Refresh tokens are not bound to the user, so Tom's expired token is renewed with ours.

vulnerabilities.title: JWT tokens: kid header SQL injection
vulnerabilities.description: kid header concatenated into SQL that loads the key, so attacker chooses the verification key.
vulnerabilities.note: Injection lives inside a JWT header and must be combined with forging a token.

vulnerabilities.title: JWT tokens: jku header key confusion
vulnerabilities.description: Server fetches the verification key from the token's jku URL, trusting attacker-hosted keys.
vulnerabilities.note: Needs an attacker-hosted JWKS (WebWolf).

vulnerabilities.title: JWT tokens: quiz
vulnerabilities.description: Quiz on JWT signature handling.

vulnerabilities.title: Password reset: email functionality with WebWolf
vulnerabilities.description: Learner receives a reset mail in WebWolf; introduces the flow.

vulnerabilities.title: Password reset: guessable security questions
vulnerabilities.description: Account recovery answer (favourite colour) is guessable for known users.

vulnerabilities.title: Password reset: the problem with security questions
vulnerabilities.description: Learner reviews which security questions are weak; nothing vulnerable.

vulnerabilities.title: Password reset: poisoned reset link
vulnerabilities.description: Reset link is built from the Host header, so the victim's token is sent to an attacker host.
vulnerabilities.note: Needs WebWolf to capture the token; scored via /PasswordReset/reset/change-password.

vulnerabilities.title: Secure Passwords
vulnerabilities.description: Learner enters a password that passes a strength estimator; nothing vulnerable.

vulnerabilities.title: Logging Security: log spoofing
vulnerabilities.description: Username written to the log unencoded, so CRLF input forges an admin login entry.

vulnerabilities.title: Logging Security: password in application log
vulnerabilities.description: Admin password is written (Base64) to the server log at startup.
vulnerabilities.note: Needs access to the server console/log.

vulnerabilities.title: Bypass front-end restrictions: field restrictions
vulnerabilities.description: Server accepts values that the form's select, radio, checkbox and maxlength controls forbid.

vulnerabilities.title: Bypass front-end restrictions: validation
vulnerabilities.description: Regex validation exists only in JavaScript; server accepts non-matching input.

vulnerabilities.title: Client side filtering: salary data
vulnerabilities.description: All employee records, including the CEO's salary, are sent to the browser and filtered client-side.

vulnerabilities.title: Client side filtering: get it for free
vulnerabilities.description: Coupon codes endpoint lists every code, including a hidden 100% discount.

vulnerabilities.title: HTML tampering: change the price
vulnerabilities.description: Order total comes from a hidden form field and is trusted by the server.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 1: Admin lost password
vulnerabilities.description: Admin password pattern plus a PIN hidden in the logo image's bytes.
vulnerabilities.note: Needs reading bytes of an image. Password template is also a constant in SolutionConstants.java (not listed separately).

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 2: Partner feed recovery (XXE to internal endpoint)
vulnerabilities.description: Feed import resolves XML external entities through a redirect to reach an internal diagnostics endpoint.
vulnerabilities.note: Chained XXE + redirect + internal endpoint.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 2: unvalidated redirect used in the chain
vulnerabilities.description: Partner 'go' endpoint issues a 302 to any URL in its url parameter.
vulnerabilities.note: GET param url. A link in the challenge chain rather than the scored flaw itself.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 5: Without password
vulnerabilities.description: Password parameter concatenated into the login query; injection logs in as Larry.
vulnerabilities.note: POST username_login/password_login; username must be exactly Larry before the query runs, so a probe with another username never reaches the sink.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 7: exposed .git
vulnerabilities.description: A .git archive of the source is downloadable from the challenge path.
vulnerabilities.note: Exact path /WebGoat/challenge/7/.git (zip as octet-stream), not the web root.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 7: predictable admin reset link
vulnerabilities.description: Reset link generator from the leaked source is predictable, giving the admin's reset link.
vulnerabilities.note: Insecure password reset token; needs the .git exposure first.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 8: Without account
vulnerabilities.description: Vote endpoint rejects GET as 'login required' but other methods (e.g. HEAD) vote and return the flag.
vulnerabilities.note: HTTP verb tampering.

vulnerabilities.title: Security exercises: flag submission
vulnerabilities.description: Endpoint where challenge flags are submitted; answer check only.

amendments.change: Added `keywords` to entries that share a location with other findings (wildcard paths, several components in one file) and a "*" path to client-library entries, because library findings point at the page that loads them.
amendments.reason: Pilot run 2 on Juice Shop and DVNA showed class-plus-location matching credited unrelated findings (any header finding for X-Powered-By, an nginx finding for the documented mongo image). Which vulnerabilities are listed and in scope did not change.
